reviews.scope_review: Conditional full-pair restoration rule after the supplied-W stress deletion, plus one exact rational noncanonical fixture.
hypotheses: A is an n-label global minimizer first contact-minimal and then actual-diameter-pair-minimal; every label, including contact isolates, remains in the ledger.

R is the supplied deletion from the canonical stress-transversal result. If R contains a contact vertex, insert k=|R| labels; if R contains only isolates, also delete an outside contact vertex and insert k+1 labels.
Every packet-internal and packet-to-retained squared distance is strictly in (1,D^2).
reviews.independent_proof_reconstruction: Cardinality is preserved. Old retained pairs are unchanged; every new pair lies strictly between both bounds, so no new contact or old-D pair is introduced. The removed nonisolated contact vertex deletes at least one old edge; the contact graph can only lose edges and remains triangle-free. If the endpoint diameter is below D, global minimality at n is contradicted. If it remains D, the first lexicographic tie-break (contact count) is contradicted; the second diameter-pair tie-break is not needed. At D, the actual-diameter graph is the old induced graph on retained labels; at D' < D, newly active pairs may occur and must be separately recorded, but do not affect the strict diameter contradiction.
reviews.falsification_and_controls: The exact 11-label fixture has p_i=(i,0), i=0..9, q=(1/2,11/10), D^2=81, nine path contacts, one D-pair, and q is a contact isolate. Deleting p0 removes the sole old-D pair; r=(8/5,11/10) restores 11 labels with every new pair strict, eight contacts, max 3673/50, and new endpoint pair p9-q. Controls: restoring p0 itself restores contact and D; weak upper margin r_w=(32/5,36/5) creates a new pair at old D; one-for-one replacement of isolate q does not reduce contacts; deleting without packet changes cardinality; the k+1 fallback deletes q and p0 and restores both.

reviews.scope_review: Finite equivalence between a strict complete-label endpoint and an independent transversal of the precisely defined conflict graph.
hypotheses: Finite planar option set O_i for every label, n>=2; strict endpoint requires 1<=|y_i-y_j|<D for all distinct labels.

reviews.head: 08442dbb7a3159ef1d0cc7ec966b99d6eced0edd
reviews.title: Independent audit: PR #948 quarter-fold face obstructions
reviews.scope_review: Conditional PR948 quarter-fold obstruction report: reflex contact release, exact-graph eight-face exclusion, and short-arc count reduction; no integrated source endpoint.
hypotheses: Finite unit-separated source with a simple bounded actual contact face and global/contact-minimal normalization for the contact-release contradiction.
For the eight-face exclusion, a full placement retains the exact old contact graph, is unit-separated, and has diameter <=D; canonical strict/weak transformed-hull covers apply.
For short-arc counts, the face is convex with four arcs of at least two edges and the folded boundary remains lower-feasible and triangle-free.
reviews.independent_proof_reconstruction: At a reflex vertex, the contact-free sector has angle >pi, so the complementary cone of incident unit-neighbor vectors has width <pi. A small displacement opposite its bisector gives negative dot product with each contact vector, opening every unit edge; noncontacts and upper pairs stay feasible by finite slack. The vertex is not a diameter endpoint (diameter endpoints are uniquely exposed), so contact deletion contradicts contact-minimality unless diameter decreases. For the eight-face fold, determinant signs make transitions strictly clockwise; convexity forces same-sign turns flat, leaving a parallelogram if the fold is nonconstant. Any bowed arc gives a nonconvex actual face after exact graph preservation and strict hull cover, contradicting contact release; flat reverse-fold plus weak cover excludes interior labels. For four arcs with turns T_i, adding adjacent transition inequalities yields T_i<pi/3; chord lengths obey (sqrt(3)/2)r_i<L_i<=r_i. Equal opposite chord lengths then exclude unequal opposite counts through total degree 18, so odd convex faces of degree <=17 have constant signs.
reviews.falsification_and_controls: The report records exact rational/Q(sqrt(15)) verifier and certificate byte comparisons; finite cases include bowed and straight mixed 8-cycles, a diameter switch, odd 21-cycle, and all arc-count vectors through degree 18. The 21-cycle is explicitly nonglobal (25-site square-grid competitor D^2<=32<58), so it blocks extrapolation. The current reviewer ran artifact-index and reading-edition checks only; those are publication checks, not the analytic verifier.
reviews.unchecked_inherited_dependencies_and_lim: Canonical endpoint extremality, local minimum-face, hull-cover and global-minimality inputs are inherited; no all-label nonaffine assignment is constructed. Scope excludes changed-contact endpoints, larger odd faces beginning at degree 19, inactive-upper control outside stated branch, and global source extraction. No full historical proof chain replay.
reviews.evidence_note: Exact report was read and proof reconstructed; this PR changes report/index/reading artifacts only. Report’s own exact verifier runs are attributed to that report, not claimed as this reviewer’s replay.

reviews.title: Target C: conditionally audit positive-leaf anchor sharpening
reviews.scope_review: Conditional positive-leaf anchor boundary-distance implication; report is PR #124. The antecedent near-diameter localization is PR #139 and is a separate unreviewed candidate.
hypotheses: Noncollinear full-source global minimum-diameter source with D large; actual diameter endpoint p with unique actual unit neighbor a.
Positive coefficient alpha>0 on contact pa in a normalized full-source KKT stress and nonnegative coefficients on actual diameter partners.
Full-source circumradius R<=D/2+eta, eta=3^(1/4)*sqrt(D).
The PR #139 endpoint-direction estimates hold for the same source at s=0 and s=2; all source labels including isolates constrain K_D.
reviews.independent_proof_reconstruction: Set n=p-a, |n|=1, and nu=(p-x)/d. For d>=D-2, PR #139 supplies transverse |(p-c)·Jnu|=O(D^(2/3)); the circumradius gives longitudinal (p-c)·nu>=d-R>=D/2-eta-2, positive for large D. The direction nu and all actual diameter normals therefore lie within epsilon=O(D^(-1/3)) of e=(p-c)/|p-c|. From alpha*n=sum beta_y(p-y), alpha>0 and beta_y>=0, n is in the positive cone of diameter normals in this arc, so n·nu>=cos(2epsilon)=1-O(D^(-2/3)). Then |a-x|^2=(d-1)^2+2d(1-n·nu) gives |a-x|<=d-1+O(D^(-2/3)) on d>=D-2; d<D-2 is covered by |a-x|<=d+1<D-1. Hence |a-x|<=D-1+delta uniformly for every source label. For the boundary step, any actual diameter midpoint z has |x-z|<=sqrt(3)D/2 by the parallelogram identity; thus K_D=intersection of all disks radius D-1 contains a ball of radius r=(1-sqrt(3)/2)D-1. Support of W_D=intersection of all radius-D disks plus K_D+B(0,1) subset W_D gives h_KD(n)<=n·a. Contract a toward z by theta=r/(r+delta): q=theta a+(1-theta)z satisfies every disk radius D-1 inequality because theta*delta=(1-theta)*r. Thus q in K_D and dist(a,partial K_D)<=|a-q|=delta/(r+delta)|a-z|=O(D^(-2/3)).
reviews.falsification_and_controls: Checked short-pair branch d<D-2 separately; angle cone aperture <pi makes the positive hull valid; alpha>0 and beta>=0 are essential; contraction is checked against every label, including isolates. No counterexample found to this conditional implication. Exact PR-head audit report includes these checks. reviews.head: 6c2b6d7be91c6d6cd5b9e2133c8add94c506bf1f
reviews.title: Audit open-cell phase-flux identity and scope conditions
reviews.scope_review: Exact open-cell phase-flux identity and conditional sign/endpoint consequences.
hypotheses: Finite cut-balance identity A_i u(theta_i)=sum_{a_h<i<=b_h} beta_h r_h with coherent phase lifts.
Sign classification requires positive KKT weight on every moving actual diameter and non-grazing finite-change estimate.
Inverse-D endpoint branch additionally requires fixed-star complete O-O slab motion, Section-90 window |u_q-u_p|<=4K/D, and contact-minimal then diameter-pair-minimal source.
reviews.independent_proof_reconstruction: Orient each cut-crossing row by sign(r_h·J u(mu)) and weight it by f_h=beta_h|r_h·J u(mu)|. Dotting cut balance with J u(mu) gives prefix divergence Phi(P_i;mu)=A_i sin(theta_i-mu). For S=P_q minus P_p and midpoint mu=(theta_p+theta_q)/2, subtraction gives exact F_out-F_in=(A_p+A_q)sin((theta_q-theta_p)/2); its slab work equals -2(A_p+A_q)t^2. With full positive support, t>0 gives both signs iff F_in>0, otherwise all moving rows shorten; t<0 is symmetric. Source ideals/sinks then force the phase-order condition if the inherited endpoint theorem excludes the inactive near-pair witness.
reviews.falsification_and_controls: Removing full positivity breaks the full-graph equivalence: a zero-weight incoming geometric diameter has opposite finite length sign while F_in=0. Dropping the Section-90 phase window and taking phase gap pi/3 gives |u_q-u_p|=1, not O(1/D). Prior finite regressions are consistent but lack vertex KKT/global-minimality; direct reviewer ran artifact-index and reading-edition checks, not those source regressions.

reviews.head: 5053e17987b1aa72173f4a656213532536b24933
reviews.title: Independent audit: PR #948 large-array boundary attachment
reviews.scope_review: Conditional PR948 large-array boundary attachment theorem for complete bent rhombic arrays with both dimensions >=delta D.
hypotheses: Actual full-source labelled complete array p_ij=z+x_i+y_j with distinct labels, unit consecutive row/column edges, strict rhombic faces, and a,c>=delta D.
Triangle-free contact-minimal global source; r counts distinct noncorner boundary vertices attached by unit contact to outside labels.
Canonical full-source circumradius and local positive-spanning/exposure facts apply.
reviews.independent_proof_reconstruction: Direction windows give only designated internal grid contacts. Opposite three-ray boundary stars with nonzero turn have exactly one non-positive-spanning vertex, hence one diameter endpoint; zero turn would make both endpoints midpoints and violates extremality. If r/D tended to zero along D->infinity, normalized piecewise-linear array paths have bounded Lipschitz constants and a subsequential limit. Good star indices are vanishing-gap meshes, forcing each path point onto one of two fixed radius-1/2 lens circles. Cell determinants enforce strict transverse monotonicity, so a path cannot switch lens circles. At the common limiting corner, tangent lines of the two circle paths must coincide, but limiting row/column angle window [pi/3,2pi/3] excludes parallel and antiparallel tangents.
